1.note: A pun: קְרָבַי "my innards" and קְרָבוֹת "battles" have the same letters.

2.note: Gen 26:21, the name of a well ("enmity"). Here it also sounds like שָׂטָן, Satan; compare "like a satan" a few lines on. The subject "he" is Time.

3.he: וְהַיֱפִי הִלְבִּישְׁךָ מִשְׁיוֹ. וְשִׁלֵּם לְךָ נִשְׁיוֹ
3.note: מֶשִׁי is silk (Ezek 16:10, 13); נְשִׁי is a debt (2 Kgs 4:7). The two words rhyme. "Paid its debt" is read as "gave you all it owed".

4.note: Num 20:5 "it is no place of seed", of the wilderness. Here the seed is also offspring: a man without a wife has no place for his seed.

5.he: לֶחְיָהּ מַעֲלָה שְׁחָרִים. וּשְׂעָרָה מַעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים
5.note: Her bright cheek is the dawn and her black hair the evening. מַעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים is the phrase of the evening prayer, said of God, "who brings on the evenings".

6.note: Two vessels of the Tabernacle: the lampstand (her shining cheek) and the jar of manna (Exod 16:33; her sweet mouth). The reading of the image is uncertain.

7.note: The edition points כְּפִירִים, "young lions" (fierce, bright eyes). Unvocalized it could also be read with כֹּפֶר, henna (Song 1:14). Uncertain.

8.note: Meant as praise (she captures hearts), but it also warns of what is to come. Uncertain.

9.note: A pun: חַכָּה "fish-hook" and חֵךְ "palate": her smooth speech (Prov 5:3) was the hook.

10.note: The edition points הַפַּחוֹת, "the governors" (Neh 2:7). Unvocalized, פחות also means "the lesser, the low": an ironic double reading.

11.note: חֲבוּרָה, "union, joining", plays on the narrator's name, Ḥever.

12.note: A pun: חַמָּה "sun" and חֵמָה "wrath" are written with the same letters.

13.note: Read as lips curled up towards the nose. יָהִינוּ is "dared" (הֵהִין, a post-biblical verb). Uncertain.

14.note: זִקִּים is "fetters" (Nah 3:10, Isa 45:14) or, as in later Hebrew, "sparks, fiery bolts" (compare Isa 50:11 זִיקוֹת). Uncertain.

15.note: In the Hebrew the word מַלְאֲכֵי "angels of" is split between the two half-lines. The English moves "the coming" to keep the halves.

16.note: Num 21:16 "and from there to Beer (the well)", from the list of the journeys in the wilderness. Here the well seems to be her belly, to which the food goes. The joke is uncertain.

17.note: יְשַׁו is read as "may He make" (from שִׁוָּה, "set, make"). The curse: may lions eat her, so that she has no grave but their bellies.
